THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 27.02.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:16587 CRL.MC NO. 1351 OF 2025 2  ORDER Petitioner is the 2nd accused in S.T No.1833 of 2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kunnamangalam.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kunnamangalam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The crime is registered alleging commission of offences punishable under Sections 3(1)(zz)(xii), 20, 26(1), 26(2)(i) and 27(1) of the Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The specific allegation in the complaint filed by the 2 nd respondent Food Safety Officer is that, at about 12.50 p.m on 12.2.2021, he inspected the premises of the food business establishment 'M/s Salmanya Supermarket' and collected the sample 'Nandini Goodlife Toned Milk'.

Later, on analysis,
the sample was found to contain 'Aflatoxin M1' to an extent of not less than 0.654 micrograms/kg,
which is above the prescribed limit as per Regulation 2.2.1 of the Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner being the licencee of the Supermarket is arrayed as the 2025:KER:16587 2nd accused, the manufacturer as the 7 th accused and the 5th accused being the person who marketed the products.
3. Heard, learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned ADGP appearing for the respondents.
4. The short question arising for consideration is whether the presence of 'Aflatoxin M1' in the sealed packet taken from a seller would attract the alleged offence.
The answer to the question can only be in the negative in view of Section 27(3), as per which the seller can be made liable only if he had received the product with the knowledge that it is unsafe.

5. Undoubtedly, the product sold by the petitioner being of a renowned manufacturer and in packed condition, he cannot therefore be attributed with the knowledge that it contained 'Aflatoxin M1'.
6.
In such circumstances, continuance of the proceedings against the petitioner will be an abuse of process of court.
In the result, all further proceedings against the petitioner 2025:KER:16587 in S.T No.1833 of 2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kunnamangalam is quashed.
